newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris broker downgrades Dior, ups Hermes.
newsitem.headline: Paris broker downgrades Dior, ups Hermes.

text.p: Paris brokerage Cheuvreux de Virieu has dropped luxury goods firm Christian Dior from its recommended list for big capitalisation stocks and replaced it with Hermes, market operators said on Friday.
Hermes moved up from the brokerage's list of small capitalisation stocks and was replaced by media group Filipacchi, they said.
Dior shares were up 0.17 percent at 601 francs at 1117 GMT, while Hermes was up 0.33 percent at 1,204. Filipacchi gained 3.86 percent to 1,049 francs. The market was up 0.18 percent at 2,107.88.
Fashion and perfume group Christian Dior is one the holding companies of luxury giant LVMH
"Cheuvreux de Virieu already has LVMH on its list of recommended big capitalisations," one operator said. "Since the news has been less than good, the broker decided to take out Dior."
Cheuvreux considers the discount on Dior has returned to normal levels, the source added.

LVMH reported this week operating profit for the first half fell to 2.62 billion francs from 2.92 billion, with a drop the contribution from the perfumes and beauty products segment to 70 million francs from 380 million.
Hermes was moved up to Cheuvreux' "big caps" list due to a strong gain in its market capitalisation, bourse sources said. The broker had already been positive on the stock.
The broker considered Filipacchi's results to be good and liked its presentation at an analysts' meeting on Thursday. It had already been positive on the stock.
Filipacchi Medias reported first-half net attributable profit of 84.99 million francs, up from 78.64 million a year ago.
